election._note: D'Hondt in a single national constituency with a 3% threshold, lowered for minority lists (0.7% for the Croat community) -- the minority relief unmodelled. Elected 11 June 2023, so the next is due by mid-2027. Law on the Election of Councillors and MPs; Wikipedia, '2023 Montenegrin parliamentary election'.

dissolution._note: The Skupština may shorten its own mandate by a majority of all MPs, and the President must dissolve it if no government is elected within 90 days (Art. 92) -- self_dissolution is the nearest single rule, the failed-formation route recorded here. Constitution of Montenegro, Arts. 84, 92.

head_of_state._note: The President, directly elected for five years, two terms at most; elected April 2023 and inaugurated in May, so the next falls in spring 2028. Constitution of Montenegro, Arts. 96-97.
head_of_state.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 156: two thirds of all MPs; amendments to the state's character, sovereignty, borders and the amendment procedure itself then need confirmation by referendum (Art. 157) with three fifths of the electorate. The two_thirds bar is carried; the entrenched tier is read as optional. Constitution of Montenegro, Arts. 156-157.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 157's referendum is mandatory for the entrenched chapters only -- a split the referendum field cannot carry. Constitution of Montenegro, Art. 157.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: No eternity clause; the form of the state sits in the referendum-gated tier, which is a higher bar and not a bar.

judicial._note: A Constitutional Court reviews the constitutionality of laws (Arts. 149-154). Constitution of Montenegro, Art. 149.

formation._note: The President proposes a Prime Minister after consulting the parliamentary groups, and the Skupština elects the government by a majority of all MPs (Art. 103). No-confidence needs a majority of all MPs (Art. 107), read as simple_present. The 2023 government is a broad coalition. Constitution of Montenegro, Arts. 103, 107.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Montenegro was a kingdom from 1910 to 1918; the restored monarch here is fictional.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/Ministry of Finance ~2024, rounded, on AUT.json's conventions. VAT 21% standard; corporate 15 is the top of the 9-15% progressive schedule; income 12 blends the 0/9/15 wage schedule; capital gains 15%; no wealth tax. Revenue ~36% of GDP includes social contributions, cut by the 2022 'Europe Now' contribution reform. Debt ~60% of GDP (end-2024), in euros: Montenegro uses the euro unilaterally and is NOT a eurozone member, which is why data/orgs/eurozone.json does not list it. Spending scaled to expenditure near 40% of GDP.
